intro: Thanksgiving Day brings Bears at Lions with first place in the NFC North on the line, then Chiefs at Bills on Thursday night. Pittsburgh released Aaron Rodgers on Wednesday, and Brock Purdy's ankle puts the 49ers' Sunday game with Seattle in doubt. 160 stories across all 32 teams.

top.label: Biggest Story
top.headline: Steelers release Aaron Rodgers after his Pat McAfee interview
top.dek: Pittsburgh benched Rodgers this week, then cut him Wednesday after he criticized coach Mike McCarthy on The Pat McAfee Show. Any team can claim him until 4 p.m. ET Thursday, and he becomes a free agent if nobody does. Mason Rudolph starts Friday against Denver.

top.label: Injury Watch
top.headline: Brock Purdy sits out practice with an ankle injury before Seattle
top.dek: Purdy hurt his ankle in the second quarter of the win over Minnesota and did not practice Wednesday. Kyle Shanahan called it a low ankle issue, not a high sprain, and said Purdy is day to day. If Purdy sits Sunday, Mac Jones starts.

top.label: Player Spotlight
top.headline: Blake Corum runs for a career-high 184 yards in the Rams' win over Green Bay
top.dek: Corum carried 32 times for 184 yards and a touchdown, and 151 of those yards came after halftime. Matthew Stafford threw only eight passes in the second half of the 26-13 win on Wednesday night.

top.label: Stat of the Day
top.headline: 5: straight games the Bears have not trailed, their first such run since 1985
top.dek: Chicago also tied a franchise record by scoring in all 20 quarters during the streak. The Bears carry it into Ford Field on Thanksgiving against a Lions team that has won six straight.

top.label: What's Next
top.headline: Bills host the Chiefs on Thanksgiving night with the AFC's top seed in play
top.dek: Buffalo plays its first Thanksgiving home game in franchise history at 8:20 PM ET on NBC, with steady rain in the forecast. The Bills have won six straight, and Kansas City's defensive coordinator expects designed quarterback runs for Josh Allen.

teams.name: Buffalo Bills
teams.headline: Bills host Chiefs on Thanksgiving night

stories.text: Bills host Chiefs on Thanksgiving night with the AFC's top seed in play
stories.summary: Buffalo hosts its first Thanksgiving game in franchise history on Thursday night, a meeting with Kansas City that carries the No. 1 seed in the AFC. The Bills have won six straight and went 3-0 in their earlier Thanksgiving games with Josh Allen. Players said the new stadium and the national stage have the building ready for a loud night.

stories.text: Five Bills carry questionable tags into Thanksgiving night
stories.summary: Cornerback Christian Benford (groin), tight end Dalton Kincaid (thumb and ankle), defensive lineman T.J. Sanders (shoulder), guard O'Cyrus Torrence (ankle) and linebacker Dorian Williams (calf) are all listed as questionable. Edge rusher Greg Rousseau and tackle Spencer Brown were limited early in the week and moved to full participation Tuesday.

stories.text: James Cook sits second in the NFL in rushing yards
stories.summary: Cook has 1,060 rushing yards, behind only Jahmyr Gibbs. He has 30 runs of 10 or more yards and averages 20.9 carries a game, and both marks rank second in the league. Buffalo wants to run early on Thursday, and Kansas City's plan starts with stopping him.

stories.text: 0: Josh Allen's rushing attempts against Miami, and Kansas City noticed
stories.summary: Allen did not run once in Sunday's 26-9 win over the Dolphins. Chiefs defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo called it a setup and said he expects Buffalo to call a good number of designed quarterback runs on Thanksgiving. Allen credited Miami's game plan for taking away his lanes.

stories.text: Chiefs at Highmark Stadium, Thursday 8:20 PM ET on NBC
stories.summary: Buffalo hosts Kansas City on Thursday at 8:20 PM ET on NBC. The forecast calls for steady rain and temperatures in the upper 30s. Watch whether the Bills run Allen and whether the defense extends its streak of three games without a touchdown allowed.

teams.name: Miami Dolphins
teams.headline: Dolphins weigh Proctor move to tackle

stories.text: Dolphins talk about moving rookie Kadyn Proctor to tackle
stories.summary: Miami has discussed shifting first-round pick Kadyn Proctor from left guard to tackle, where he could replace the struggling Austin Jackson on the right side. Coach Jeff Hafley says the move is under consideration. The Dolphins fell to 1-9 after a 26-9 loss at Buffalo.

stories.text: Malik Willis waits to see if core injury heals on its own
stories.summary: Quarterback Malik Willis remains on injured reserve with a core muscle injury, and the team is waiting to learn whether it heals without surgery. He must miss at least two more games. Linebacker Ronnie Harrison Jr. has opened his practice window to return from injured reserve. Reports on defensive tackle Zach Sieler conflict, with one source calling him out for the season and a Miami Herald headline saying he is poised to return.

stories.text: Kyle McCord gets another start after a rough day in Buffalo
stories.summary: McCord went 12 of 33 for 102 yards with an interception against the Bills. He took two sacks and eight hits. Hafley said the practice reps and the chemistry he has built with the line and receivers should help, and McCord is expected to start at least two more games.

stories.text: 31st: Dolphins slip in the Week 12 power rankings
stories.summary: Miami ranks 31st in the Palm Beach Post's Week 12 power rankings after the loss to Buffalo, which sits first at 9-1. The Dolphins have lost four straight and are 1-9.

stories.text: Jets visit Hard Rock Stadium, Sunday 1 PM ET on CBS
stories.summary: Miami hosts the New York Jets on Sunday at 1 PM ET on CBS. The Dolphins beat the Jets earlier this season, on Oct. 25, and have not rushed for 100 yards since. Watch the pass protection and whether the rookie receivers stop dropping passes.

teams.name: New England Patriots
teams.headline: Maye out, DeVito starts at the Chargers

stories.text: Vrabel names Tommy DeVito the starter after Drake Maye's fibula fracture
stories.summary: Maye fractured his right fibula in the loss to Detroit in Munich, and his return this season is uncertain. Coach Mike Vrabel said the team will not look outside the building and called DeVito the starter. Rookie Behren Morton moves up to the No. 2 spot.

stories.text: A.J. Brown's hamstring adds to a long list of missed games
stories.summary: Brown has missed six of New England's first 10 games, first with a high ankle sprain, then with a knee issue. He left the Detroit game with a hamstring injury. Executive Eliot Wolf said the team knew about a degenerative knee condition before the trade. Maye remains on the active roster, not injured reserve, because the Patriots are close to their limit of return designations.

stories.text: Tommy DeVito steps in with a short run of game snaps
stories.summary: DeVito replaced Maye in the first quarter against the Lions and finished 12 of 24 for 81 yards with a touchdown and an interception. He started all three preseason games and threw for 344 yards and three touchdowns without an interception. Vrabel wants him to manage the offense and keep the tempo steady.

stories.text: 18: touchdown passes Drake Maye threw before the injury
stories.summary: Maye entered the Detroit game with 18 touchdown passes, 8.4 yards per attempt and a 74.2 Total QBR, all in the NFL's top five. He also had 219 rushing yards and three rushing touchdowns, top five among quarterbacks. DeVito now runs an offense built around that production.

stories.text: At the Chargers, Sunday 4:05 PM ET on CBS
stories.summary: New England visits the Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday at 4:05 PM ET on CBS. Vrabel said he could not imagine Maye playing. After the Chargers, the Patriots host Buffalo in Week 13, so the AFC East race is close to the front of the schedule.

teams.name: New York Jets
teams.headline: Jets end five-game skid in Los Angeles

stories.text: Jets beat the Chargers 27-24 to end a five-game losing streak
stories.summary: New York won in Inglewood behind three touchdown passes from Geno Smith. Coach Aaron Glenn praised a balanced offense that scored in the red zone. Rookie David Bailey added two sacks and sits at 9.5 on the season.

stories.text: Two Jets receivers practice limited or sit out Wednesday
stories.summary: Isaiah Williams (ribs) was limited Wednesday after missing last week. Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle) did not practice and Glenn called him day to day. Smith played through an ankle injury against the Chargers.

stories.text: Geno Smith went 17 of 21 with three touchdowns
stories.summary: Smith threw three touchdown passes against the Chargers. Through 11 games his 68 percent completion rate ranks second in team history and his 102.7 passer rating is the best. He has the fewest interceptions of any Jets quarterback over that span.

stories.text: 0: punts, turnovers, failed fourth downs and missed field goals
stories.summary: The Jets recorded zeros in all four categories against the Chargers, a first for the franchise in a single game. It was also their second game this season without a punt. The defense piled up six sacks of Justin Herbert.

stories.text: At the Dolphins, Sunday 1 PM ET on CBS
stories.summary: The Jets play at Miami on Sunday at 1 PM ET on CBS. The Dolphins are 1-9 and have lost four straight, though they beat New York earlier this season. Watch the Jets' clock management, which one writer flagged as a problem after the Chargers win.

teams.name: Baltimore Ravens
teams.headline: Ravens carry a six-game skid to Houston

stories.text: Ravens carry a six-game losing streak into Houston
stories.summary: Baltimore lost 35-33 at Carolina on Sunday, its sixth defeat in a row. Lamar Jackson remains out and Tyler Huntley is on injured reserve, so Jacoby Brissett keeps the job. Brissett has thrown for at least 275 yards in both starts since the Nov. 6 trade, but he has an interception in each and the Ravens lost both close games.

stories.text: Derrick Henry back in concussion protocol
stories.summary: Coach Jesse Minter said Wednesday that Henry re-entered the concussion protocol. Henry left the Carolina game after saying his bell was rung, then tested clear, and the team placed him back in protocol as a precaution. Minter said he expects Henry to be back for Houston.

stories.text: Henry runs for 94 and a score in a losing effort
stories.summary: Henry carried for 94 yards and a touchdown against Carolina, his best game in a while. He ranks seventh in the NFL with 793 rushing yards. He also owns 1,611 yards and 14 touchdowns in 16 career games against Houston, the team he faces Sunday.

stories.text: 11.5: sacks for Will Anderson Jr., the most in the NFL
stories.summary: Houston's edge rusher leads the league in sacks and added a safety in last week's 26-3 win over Indianapolis. Baltimore has to protect Brissett against that rush, and the Ravens have not found an answer for pressure during this skid. The Texans beat them 44-10 in the last meeting.

stories.text: At Houston, Sunday 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: Baltimore (4-7) visits Houston (4-6) in Week 12. The Ravens lead the all-time series 13-3, but Houston won the last meeting. Watch whether the run game, which averages 128.5 yards a game, can lean on Henry if he clears protocol.

teams.name: Cincinnati Bengals
teams.headline: Bengals try to reset after Monday night loss

stories.text: Bengals look to reset after loss ends five-game win streak
stories.summary: Washington beat Cincinnati 22-20 on Monday night, ending the Bengals' five-game winning streak. Joe Burrow said he wished he had about four plays back and that the team did not do enough to win. A win Sunday over the 3-7 Saints would put Cincinnati at 8-3.

stories.text: Risner day to day with knee issues
stories.summary: Right guard Dalton Risner (knees) is day to day, and Zac Taylor said the team will decide on Sunday. Risner did only a walkthrough Wednesday, and Jalen Rivers played 58 snaps in his place against Washington. Safety Bryan Cook hurt his ankle in the first half Monday, played 64 snaps and is only sore.

stories.text: Burrow throws for 300 in the loss
stories.summary: Burrow went 28 of 40 for 300 yards and two touchdowns against Washington. The Commanders held Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins to 74 receiving yards combined. Burrow praised the Saints defense, which has not allowed more than 22 points in a game since mid-October.

stories.text: 31: rushing yards on 14 carries against Washington
stories.summary: The Bengals could not run the ball Monday night, and the lack of a ground game narrowed the offense. Shemar Stewart also played no snaps on defense in the loss. Taylor said that came from game flow and that he expects to give Stewart more chances.

stories.text: Saints at Paycor Stadium, Sunday 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: Cincinnati hosts New Orleans in Week 12 on a normal week after a short turnaround. The Saints bring two top-ten pass rushers in Carl Granderson (8.5 sacks) and Chase Young (8). Bengals offensive coordinator Dan Pitcher expects a physical game.

teams.name: Cleveland Browns
teams.headline: Browns get a Sunday night stage at home

stories.text: Browns flexed into Sunday Night Football after bye
stories.summary: The NFL moved Cleveland's Week 12 home game against the Raiders to prime time. The Browns are 4-0 at Huntington Bank Field, their first unbeaten home start since 1963, and every one of those wins came by three points. They return from the Week 11 bye still inside the AFC playoff field.

stories.text: Raheim Sanders returns to practice from injured reserve
stories.summary: The Browns designated running back Raheim Sanders for return Tuesday, and he can practice again. He hurt his hip in Week 5 and had nine carries for 43 yards and 11 catches for 74 yards before the injury. He is expected to work as the third back behind Quinshon Judkins and Dylan Sampson.

stories.text: Deshaun Watson keeps winning late
stories.summary: Watson has six game-winning drives this season, which makes Cleveland dangerous in close games. The Browns beat Houston 27-24 on Nov. 15 with another fourth-quarter comeback. He has said his future in Cleveland is up to his agent, and 2026 is the last year of his original deal.

stories.text: 29.7: points per game the Raiders allow, most in the NFL
stories.summary: Las Vegas ranks 32nd in scoring defense and 31st against the run at 149.5 yards a game. Cleveland scores 18.8 points a game, 27th in the league, and runs for 97.5 yards a game, 24th. The matchup gives the Browns offense a rare soft spot.

stories.text: Raiders at Huntington Bank Field, Sunday 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC
stories.summary: Cleveland (6-4) hosts Las Vegas on Sunday Night Football, with rookie Fernando Mendoza, the No. 1 pick, starting for the Raiders. The Browns pass defense allows 201.1 yards a game, sixth in the NFL. They also face the Bengals at home in Week 13.

teams.name: Pittsburgh Steelers
teams.headline: Steelers cut Rodgers, Rudolph starts Friday

stories.text: Steelers release Aaron Rodgers after interview
stories.summary: Pittsburgh benched Rodgers this week, then released him Wednesday after he criticized coach Mike McCarthy on The Pat McAfee Show. Rodgers said he is not going back to Pittsburgh. Any team could claim him until 4 p.m. ET Thursday, and he becomes a free agent if nobody does.

stories.text: No new injury news as quarterback change dominates
stories.summary: None of the articles I read listed a new Steelers injury designation this week. Rodgers' absence was a coaching decision, not an injury, according to ESPN's sources. The official Friday injury report should confirm who is available against Denver.

stories.text: Mason Rudolph takes over against Denver
stories.summary: Rudolph, 31, has 20 career starts and a 9-10-1 record, and he is 1-5 in his last six starts dating to 2024. This season he has played 19 snaps and completed 1 of 4 passes for 2 yards. He has never faced Denver or a defense coached by Vance Joseph.

stories.text: 257: yards lost to sacks by Rodgers, most in the NFL
stories.summary: Rodgers took 31 sacks this season, already more than the 29 he took last year, and completed 60.9 percent of his passes. ESPN's numbers also put his off-target rate at 18.9 percent, 28th among 30 qualified passers. The Steelers lost 19-16 to Philadelphia in Week 11.

stories.text: Broncos at Acrisure Stadium, Friday 3 p.m. ET on Prime Video
stories.summary: Pittsburgh plays Denver on Black Friday in a game that matters for AFC seeding. The Broncos are chasing a seventh straight win. Watch how Rudolph handles a Vance Joseph defense and whether the running game carries the offense.

teams.name: Houston Texans
teams.headline: Texans stay alive in the AFC race

stories.text: Texans stay in the playoff chase after a rout of Indianapolis
stories.summary: Houston beat the Colts 26-3 on Thursday night and sits ninth in the AFC at 4-6. NFL Next Gen Stats gives the Texans a 34 percent chance at the playoffs. The run game has improved with tackle Braden Smith and rookie tight end Marlin Klein back in the lineup.

stories.text: Woody Marks and Marvin Harrison Jr. return to practice
stories.summary: Running back Woody Marks (concussion) and receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. (hamstring) both practiced Wednesday after missing the Colts game. Marks still has to clear the concussion protocol. Defensive end Danielle Hunter (hamstring), tackle Sheldon Rankins (ankle), receiver Kayshon Boutte (hip), tight end Brevin Jordan and guard Keylan Rutledge did not practice.

stories.text: C.J. Stroud throws three touchdowns in the win over Indy
stories.summary: Stroud completed 21 of 27 passes for 194 yards and three touchdowns against the Colts. The Texans scored 26 points while the Colts managed three. Indianapolis pulled Daniel Jones for Anthony Richardson Sr. with under eight minutes left.

stories.text: 107: David Montgomery gave Houston its first 100-yard rusher
stories.summary: Montgomery ran 26 times for a season-high 107 yards against Indianapolis. He is the first Texans back to reach 100 yards this season. It was his best game since the opener, and he returned from a groin injury that cost him about a month.

stories.text: Ravens visit Houston on Sunday
stories.summary: Houston hosts Baltimore on Sunday, Nov. 29 at 1 p.m. ET on CBS. Watch whether Marks is cleared to share the backfield with Montgomery. Hunter has missed two games and the pass rush needs him.

teams.name: Indianapolis Colts
teams.headline: Colts cut Jones, hand job to Richardson

stories.text: Colts waive Daniel Jones and name Anthony Richardson the starter
stories.summary: A day after a 26-3 loss to Houston, Indianapolis waived Jones and handed the job to Richardson. Jones signed a two-year, $88 million extension in March. Coach Shane Steichen called it a decision made for the best interest of both parties.

stories.text: Rookie end Caden Curry is done for the season
stories.summary: Curry tore a ligament in his wrist against Houston and landed on injured reserve after surgery. Cornerback Cam Taylor-Britt practiced fully and could be activated Sunday, and Sauce Gardner and tackle Bernhard Raimann are back at full speed. Receiver Alec Pierce says he partially tore his Achilles and hopes to return before the season ends.

stories.text: Anthony Richardson gets a full week as the starter
stories.summary: Richardson, the No. 4 pick in 2023, is 8-7 as a starter in his career. He lost the job to Jones in 2025, and the Colts found no trade partner when he asked out in February. He says he has improved his preparation and work habits and wants to show it Sunday.

stories.text: 13: Jones led the league in interceptions before the Colts let him go
stories.summary: Jones threw 13 interceptions and seven touchdowns in 11 games, with five fumbles and 16 giveaways. He went 3-8 as the starter. Against Houston he finished 12 of 27 for 144 yards with a 45.9 passer rating.

stories.text: Colts host the Giants with Richardson under center
stories.summary: Indianapolis plays the New York Giants on Sunday, Nov. 29 at 1 p.m. ET on Fox. The secondary is thin, so a Taylor-Britt activation would help. Watch the tackle spots, where the Colts signed Wanya Morris for depth.

teams.name: Jacksonville Jaguars
teams.headline: Jags look to bounce back against Tennessee

stories.text: Jaguars drop a 23-18 game to the Giants but still lead the South
stories.summary: Trevor Lawrence called his own play poor, and coach Liam Coen took the blame for red zone calls and a missed fourth-down chance. Jacksonville stays on top of the AFC South at 7-3. It was the team's third loss in its past 18 regular season games.

stories.text: Running back Bhayshul Tuten sits out Wednesday practice
stories.summary: Tuten (ankle/foot) did not practice Wednesday. Nine Jaguars were limited, including receiver Jakobi Meyers (ankle), guard Patrick Mekari (back), center Robert Hainsey (knee) and tackle Walker Little (knee). No game designations were out yet.

stories.text: Trevor Lawrence throws for 301 yards in a rough day
stories.summary: Lawrence went 25 of 47 for 301 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions against the Giants. He took three sacks and 11 more hits. He entered the game with 21 touchdowns and five interceptions in nine games.

stories.text: 1: Jacksonville scored one touchdown in six red zone trips
stories.summary: The Jaguars reached the red zone six times against the Giants and settled for four field goals and a turnover on downs. Their red zone touchdown rate fell from 64.3 percent to 55.9 percent. Coen said he should have run the ball more.

stories.text: Titans visit EverBank Stadium on Sunday
stories.summary: Jacksonville hosts Tennessee on Sunday, Nov. 29 at 1 p.m. ET on Fox. The Jaguars won the first meeting 40-23 in Nashville, with Lawrence throwing for 352 yards and three touchdowns. Tuten's ankle is the practice report to watch.

teams.name: Tennessee Titans
teams.headline: Titans' defense bleeds points at 1-9

stories.text: Saleh says he has 100 percent support at 1-9
stories.summary: After a 51-30 loss at Dallas, coach Robert Saleh said owner Amy Adams Strunk and the organization back him fully. The Titans have allowed 40 or more points in three straight games. That ties them with only six teams in the Super Bowl era.

stories.text: Moore, Flott and Burgess miss Wednesday practice
stories.summary: Left tackle Dan Moore Jr. (knee), cornerback Cor'Dale Flott (neck) and safety Terrell Burgess (knee) did not practice. Lineman John Franklin-Myers (back) was limited. Guard Fernando Carmona Jr. returned to practice, and receiver Carnell Tate (shoulder) was full.

stories.text: Cam Ward posts a 117.1 passer rating in a loss
stories.summary: Ward went 21 of 30 for 248 yards and two touchdowns against Dallas and added a rushing score. He took five sacks and lost a fumble. Rookie receiver Carnell Tate caught a 59-yard touchdown.

stories.text: 1,940: yards Tennessee has allowed over its last four games
stories.summary: That is the most in any four-game stretch in franchise history. The Titans gave up 485 yards and 40.3 points per game in that span. Through the first six games they allowed 343 yards and 21.5 points.

stories.text: Titans visit Jacksonville on Sunday
stories.summary: Tennessee plays at Jacksonville on Sunday, Nov. 29 at 1 p.m. ET on Fox. The Jaguars won the first meeting 40-23. Watch whether the Titans can slow Trevor Lawrence and the Jaguars' offense.

teams.name: Denver Broncos
teams.headline: Payton benches Dobbins for Black Friday trip

stories.text: Payton suspends J.K. Dobbins for the Steelers game
stories.summary: Sean Payton announced Tuesday that running back J.K. Dobbins will miss Friday's game at Pittsburgh for conduct detrimental to the team. Dobbins left the facility Tuesday and will not practice or take part in team activities this week. Payton declined to add any detail. Dobbins had one carry for no gain in Sunday's 38-24 win over the Raiders.

stories.text: Badie returns from IR as Harvey stays out
stories.summary: Tyler Badie came off injured reserve and was a full participant in practice, so he is in line to help the backfield Friday. RJ Harvey (knee) is not eligible to return until next week. Receiver Pat Bryant (ankle) is practicing in full and should be able to play.

stories.text: Rookie Jonah Coleman runs for three scores
stories.summary: Jonah Coleman, a fourth-round pick out of Washington, carried 24 times for 111 yards and three touchdowns against Las Vegas. He is the first Bronco since Mike Anderson in 2005 to run for 100 yards and three scores in one game. He also broke two tackles at the goal line to put Denver ahead 24-17, and he took 24 of the team's 27 running back carries.

stories.text: 38: Denver's season high in points, and a sixth straight win
stories.summary: The Broncos scored 38 against Las Vegas, their most this season. They have now scored at least 26 points in four straight games, their first run like that since 2024. Ja'Quan McMillian added a 35-yard interception return for a touchdown, and the defense sacked Fernando Mendoza five times.

stories.text: Denver visits Pittsburgh on Black Friday
stories.summary: The Broncos play at the Steelers on Friday at Acrisure Stadium, with kickoff at 3 p.m. ET on Prime Video. Watch who carries the load with Dobbins out and Coleman coming off 24 carries. Denver is 8-2 and sits atop the AFC West.

teams.name: Kansas City Chiefs
teams.headline: Chiefs visit Bills on Thanksgiving night

stories.text: Chiefs and Bills meet with AFC seeding on the line
stories.summary: Kansas City (8-2) plays at Buffalo (9-1) tonight, and the Bills lead the Chiefs by one game in the standings. The result could shape home-field advantage in the AFC playoffs. Josh Allen is 5-1 against Kansas City in the regular season and 0-4 in the postseason.

stories.text: Walker is out, Mahomes and Rice are cleared
stories.summary: Running back Kenneth Walker III will miss tonight's game with a groin injury. Patrick Mahomes (knee, right elbow) and receiver Rashee Rice (knee) came off the injury report Wednesday and are set to play. Tight end Noah Gray is questionable.

stories.text: Emmett Johnson keeps starting in Walker's place
stories.summary: Rookie Emmett Johnson, a fifth-round pick from Nebraska, has opened back-to-back games with at least 22 carries and 101 rushing yards. He has 314 scrimmage yards while filling in. Offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy said Walker remains the starter when healthy, but Johnson gets the job again tonight.

stories.text: 13: Mahomes' touchdown passes in November, with no picks
stories.summary: Patrick Mahomes has thrown 13 touchdowns this month without an interception and has four picks all season. The Chiefs pass rush has 11 sacks over the last three games. Buffalo's Allen has nine interceptions, so the turnover margin is worth watching.

stories.text: At Buffalo tonight, 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC
stories.summary: Kansas City plays the Bills on Thursday night at Highmark Stadium, kickoff 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC. Buffalo runs the ball better than anyone, second in the league at 146.9 yards per game with 21 rushing touchdowns. The Chiefs own the league's top red zone defense, allowing touchdowns on 36 percent of trips.

teams.name: Las Vegas Raiders
teams.headline: Mendoza gets first prime-time start in Cleveland

stories.text: Mendoza faces Cleveland in his first prime-time start
stories.summary: Rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza, the No. 1 pick in April, starts Sunday night at Cleveland with an 0-2 record as a starter. Only 20 No. 1 overall picks since 1966 have lost their first two starts. Las Vegas has dropped three straight and seven of its last eight after opening 3-0.

stories.text: Bowers is a decent bet to return from ankle and quad
stories.summary: Tight end Brock Bowers has been dealing with ankle and quadriceps injuries and was a game-time call last Sunday. He was limited Wednesday, his quad is no longer a worry, and he is tentatively on track to play. Tight end Michael Mayer, who hurt his back against Denver, practiced in full.

stories.text: Ashton Jeanty breaks a 68-yard catch against Denver
stories.summary: Running back Ashton Jeanty rushed 11 times for 79 yards and caught five passes for 90 yards in the loss to Denver. One of those catches went 68 yards for a touchdown. Wideout Jack Bech also had a strong day with eight catches on nine targets for 89 yards and a score.

stories.text: 29.7: points per game the Raiders give up, last in the NFL
stories.summary: Las Vegas allows 29.7 points a game, the worst mark in the league. Denver scored 38 on them Sunday,. The Raiders still lead the all-time series with Cleveland 18-11 and have won five of the last six meetings.

stories.text: At Cleveland on Sunday night, then a bye
stories.summary: The Raiders visit the Browns on Sunday at 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC. Cleveland is 6-4 and holds the AFC's sixth seed, and Deshaun Watson has topped 300 passing yards in his last three starts. Las Vegas has its bye in Week 13, then hosts the Chargers in Week 14.

teams.name: Los Angeles Chargers
teams.headline: Herbert in concussion protocol at 1-9

stories.text: Herbert enters concussion protocol after the Jets loss
stories.summary: Justin Herbert reported symptoms after the 27-24 loss to the Jets, and Jim Harbaugh said he is in the league's concussion protocol. Herbert must clear five phases before he can return, and no game status is set for Sunday. If he sits, D.J. Uiagalelei is next up and Jake Browning moves up from the practice squad.

stories.text: Mitchell and Mesidor are being monitored
stories.summary: Running back Keaton Mitchell hurt his knee early against the Jets, returned, and played four snaps. Edge Akheem Mesidor left with an ankle injury after 12 defensive snaps. Linebacker Daiyan Henley (knee) and Tarheeb Still missed the Jets game, and Harbaugh will see how Still's week goes.

stories.text: Omarion Hampton leads a run game that works
stories.summary: Omarion Hampton ran 14 times for 89 yards against the Jets. He has 563 yards and four rushing touchdowns on 138 carries this season. The Chargers ran for 158 yards on 30 carries in that game.

stories.text: 318: rushing yards in two games, most in the NFL
stories.summary: The Chargers have run for 318 yards over their last two games, more than any team in the league. The defense gave it back, allowing 5.8 yards per play and converting nine of 11 third downs for the Jets, per Harbaugh. Los Angeles is 1-9.

stories.text: Patriots visit SoFi Sunday at 4:05 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: The Chargers host New England on Sunday at 1:05 p.m. PT (4:05 p.m. ET) on CBS. The Patriots will be without Drake Maye, who has a fractured fibula and is expected to miss at least six weeks. Tommy DeVito is projected to start, so this could be a backup quarterback matchup.

teams.name: Dallas Cowboys
teams.headline: Cowboys host Eagles on Thanksgiving

stories.text: Cowboys chase a second straight win on Thanksgiving
stories.summary: Dallas hosts Philadelphia today after scoring 40 on San Francisco and 51 on Tennessee. The Cowboys have not won back-to-back games since last Thanksgiving, but they have won four straight on the holiday. Dallas sits at 5-6 and trails the Giants in the NFC East.

stories.text: Four Cowboys out for Thanksgiving, two questionable
stories.summary: Guard Tyler Booker (ankle), tight end Jake Ferguson (knee/ankle), safety P.J. Locke III (concussion) and receiver Jonathan Mingo (ankle) are out. All four missed Week 11 too. Cornerback Devin Moore (hip) and safety Jalen Thompson (hamstring) are questionable. Moore has not played this season.

stories.text: Dak Prescott keeps putting up 300-yard, five-touchdown games
stories.summary: Prescott has thrown for at least 300 yards and five touchdowns in each of his last two games. He is the fourth quarterback in NFL history to do that in consecutive games. Defensive tackle Quinnen Williams has also piled up seven sacks in his last six games.

stories.text: 91: points Dallas has scored in its last two games
stories.summary: The Cowboys put up 40 on the 49ers and 51 on the Titans. They have scored at least 27 points in each of their last five games. The defense is the other side of it: Dallas gave up 46 to San Francisco and 30 to Tennessee.

stories.text: Cowboys host Eagles today at 4:30 PM ET on Fox
stories.summary: Dallas plays Philadelphia on Thursday at 4:30 p.m. ET on Fox. Watch whether the Cowboys can slow the run, since they allow 5.2 yards per carry. Philadelphia has 11 sacks over its last two games, so Prescott's protection matters too.

teams.name: New York Giants
teams.headline: Giants lead NFC East after Jaguars win

stories.text: Giants beat Jaguars 23-18 and hold the NFC East lead
stories.summary: New York beat Jacksonville 23-18 at MetLife Stadium on Nov. 22. Jacksonville had been the pick to hand the Giants their fourth loss. The Giants now lead the division and travel to Indianapolis on Sunday.

stories.text: Abdul Carter is day-to-day with an ankle and calf issue
stories.summary: Carter did not practice Wednesday, but coach John Harbaugh said he should be fine for Sunday. Defensive tackle Shelby Harris and cornerback Dru Phillips also sat out with illness. Tight end Isaiah Likely (groin) and linebacker Arvell Reese (back) were limited. One report says cornerback Greg Newsome II is out at least a month.

stories.text: Abdul Carter wins NFC Defensive Player of the Week
stories.summary: Carter had two sacks, five quarterback hits and 12 pressures against Jacksonville. It was his first weekly award. Through 10 starts he has 26 tackles, five for loss, 13 quarterback hits and four sacks.

stories.text: 38.4%: the Giants blitz more than all but four teams
stories.summary: New York ranks fifth in the league in blitz rate. That pressure faces Colts quarterback Anthony Richardson on Sunday. Indianapolis is tied for fourth in passing touchdowns allowed with 19.

stories.text: Giants visit the Colts Sunday at 1 PM ET on Fox
stories.summary: New York plays at Indianapolis on Sunday, Nov. 29, at 1 p.m. ET on Fox. The Colts are 3-8. Watch Carter's availability and how the Giants cover with Newsome reportedly out.

teams.name: Philadelphia Eagles
teams.headline: Joe Milton faces old team on Thanksgiving

stories.text: Joe Milton returns to Dallas as the Eagles' starter
stories.summary: Jalen Hurts is on injured reserve and out for the season, so Milton starts at Dallas today. The Cowboys left him on their practice squad and Philadelphia signed him. The Eagles are 3-7 after beating Pittsburgh 19-16 coming off their bye, ending a seven-game losing streak.

stories.text: Eagles without Ebiketie and Jonathan Jones in Dallas
stories.summary: Outside linebacker Arnold Ebiketie (oblique) and cornerback Jonathan Jones (ankle) are out. Cornerback Quinyon Mitchell carries no designation after a limited Tuesday. An earlier report had ruled him out, so his status conflicts across sources.

stories.text: Saquon Barkley has scored in four straight games
stories.summary: Barkley's four-game touchdown streak is a career high. He had a season-high 61 rushing yards before contact against Pittsburgh. He is the main weapon for a Philadelphia offense that managed 214 yards in that win.

stories.text: 11: sacks for the Eagles over their last two games
stories.summary: Philadelphia also has 15 quarterback hits in that span. Jonathan Greenard is getting healthier and Nolan Smith Jr. is rising. Defensive coordinator Vic Fangio called Dak Prescott the hardest guy in the league to sack.

stories.text: Eagles at Cowboys today, 4:30 PM ET on Fox
stories.summary: Philadelphia plays at Dallas on Thursday at 4:30 p.m. ET on Fox. Watch Milton against his old team and the pass rush against Prescott. After that the Eagles visit Arizona in Week 13.

teams.name: Washington Commanders
teams.headline: Daniels' late drive beats Bengals 22-20

stories.text: Commanders rally past Bengals 22-20 on Monday night
stories.summary: Washington trailed 20-19 after a 56-yard Cincinnati field goal and started its last drive at its own 28 with 46 seconds left. Jayden Daniels hit rookie Antonio Williams twice for 64 yards, and Drew Stevens kicked the winning 26-yard field goal. It was the Commanders' second straight win.

stories.text: Amik Robertson and Dalton Risner questionable for Arizona
stories.summary: Cornerback Amik Robertson and Dalton Risner are listed as questionable. Daron Payne, Dyami Brown, Jeremy McNichols, Jalen Davis and Oren Burks are on injured reserve.

stories.text: Rookie Antonio Williams catches 9 passes for 122 yards
stories.summary: Williams led all receivers against Cincinnati and caught both big passes on the winning drive. Daniels finished 23-of-35 for 289 yards. Jacory Croskey-Merritt added 13 carries for 54 yards and a touchdown.

stories.text: 5: straight field goals by Drew Stevens on Washington's last five scoring drives
stories.summary: Washington opened with four punts on four possessions, then scored on six straight drives. Stevens kicked field goals on the final five of those. The Commanders also controlled the clock in the second half.

stories.text: Commanders visit the Cardinals Sunday at 4:25 PM ET on Fox
stories.summary: Washington plays at Arizona on Sunday, Nov. 29, at 4:25 p.m. ET on Fox. The Cardinals are 3-8, have lost three straight and fired defensive coordinator Nick Rallis. Quarterback Carson Beck is questionable.

teams.name: Chicago Bears
teams.headline: Bears hit Detroit with first place on the line

stories.text: Bears and Lions meet at 8-2 with the NFC North lead at stake
stories.summary: Chicago carries a five-game winning streak into Ford Field on Thanksgiving, and the winner takes sole possession of first place. Detroit has won six straight. Only three times in 193 meetings have both teams sat at least six games over .500.

stories.text: Gordon, Hicks and Johnson out for Thanksgiving
stories.summary: Cornerback Kyler Gordon (shoulder), safety Elijah Hicks (concussion) and running back Roschon Johnson (ankle) are ruled out. Hicks and Johnson both play key special teams roles. Cornerback Tyrique Stevenson (groin) and linebacker D'Marco Jackson (elbow) are questionable.

stories.text: Jeffery Simmons turns the trade into a defensive reset
stories.summary: The defensive tackle came from Tennessee on Oct. 29 and already has 5.0 sacks, tied for the team lead. Three of them came against the Saints. He now plays his first Thanksgiving game as a pro.

stories.text: 5: straight games the Bears have not trailed, their first such run since 1985
stories.summary: Caleb Williams has not lost a game he started and finished this season. Chicago also tied a franchise record by scoring in all 20 quarters during the streak. The Bears did lose some of their edge last week, when a 16-0 lead over the Saints shrank to a 21-13 final.

stories.text: At Detroit, Thursday, 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: Chicago visits Ford Field for the Thanksgiving game, with Bears favored by 2.5 on one book's opening line. Watch Detroit's outside-zone running game against a Bears run defense that gives up 4.5 yards a carry. Ben Johnson also faces his former team, where he is winless since leaving.

teams.name: Detroit Lions
teams.headline: Lions refuse to blame injuries before Bears game

stories.text: Dan Campbell rejects the injury excuse as Lions face Bears
stories.summary: Detroit has lost end Aidan Hutchinson for the season and linebacker Jack Campbell to a neck injury, and the coach says he will not wallow. He said the remaining players must cover for the missing ones. The Lions host Chicago on Thanksgiving with first place in the division at stake.

stories.text: Hutchinson done for year, Joseph back on a pitch count
stories.summary: Hutchinson tore his ACL celebrating a sack of Drake Maye, his second season-ending injury in three years. Jack Campbell has movement in his lower body after a severe neck injury, but a return this season is a long shot. Safety Kerby Joseph was set to return from his knee injury on a pitch count. This report dates to Nov. 18, so check Thursday's final designations.

stories.text: Jahmyr Gibbs leads the league in rushing and touchdowns
stories.summary: Gibbs has 1,098 rushing yards, 13 rushing touchdowns, 1,502 scrimmage yards and 15 total touchdowns. All four figures lead the NFL. He is the centerpiece of an offense that scores about 28.8 points a game.

stories.text: 14.4: points per game the Lions allow over their last five
stories.summary: Detroit gave up 29.6 points a game in its first five contests. The defense tightened up even after losing Hutchinson and Campbell, with safeties Brian Branch and Kerby Joseph back in the lineup. The Lions are 6-0 at home.

stories.text: Bears at Ford Field, Thursday, 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: Detroit hosts Chicago in the Thanksgiving opener. The Lions have lost eight of their last nine Thanksgiving games, but they own four straight wins over the Bears at Ford Field. Watch how a thin pass rush handles Caleb Williams.

teams.name: Green Bay Packers
teams.headline: Packers fade late in Thanksgiving Eve loss to Rams

stories.text: Rams run past Packers 26-13 and take the tiebreaker
stories.summary: Green Bay erased a 10-point deficit to tie the game at halftime, then got shut out 13-0 in the second half. Both teams entered at 6-4, and the Rams now hold the head-to-head edge in the wild-card race. Matt LaFleur called the rest of the schedule a one-game season.

stories.text: Christian Watson in concussion protocol after sideline hit
stories.summary: Watson had four catches for 65 yards and a touchdown before a hit to the head late in the first half. LaFleur said Watson seems to be in a good place but did not know where he stands in the protocol. He could miss Week 13 if he does not clear it.

stories.text: Micah Parsons returns from knee injury with a sack
stories.summary: Parsons played on a snap count in his first game back from the knee injury that sidelined him in December. He recorded a sack late in the first half and added several pressures. Green Bay needs that pass rush to hold up with six games left.

stories.text: 55: total yards the Packers gathered in the second half
stories.summary: The offense produced two first downs after halftime, and Jordan Love threw two interceptions that he called bad reads. The Rams ran 71 plays to Green Bay's 44 and held the ball for 40:40. Blake Corum ran 32 times for 184 yards.

stories.text: At Saints, Dec. 6, 1 p.m. ET on FOX
stories.summary: Green Bay plays at the Caesars Superdome in Week 13. The Packers lead the all-time series 19-10. Watch Watson's protocol status and whether the offense fixes its second-half problems.

teams.name: Minnesota Vikings
teams.headline: Vikings try to reset after Mexico City blowout

stories.text: Vikings need a response after 35-10 loss to the 49ers
stories.summary: Minnesota trailed 28-10 at halftime in Mexico City after Kirk Cousins threw a pick-six and the defense allowed three first-half touchdowns. The Vikings started 6-0 and have lost three of their last four. They come home to face Atlanta.

stories.text: Darrisaw sore, five Vikings estimated out of Wednesday walk-through
stories.summary: Left tackle Christian Darrisaw is dealing with soreness, and Kevin O'Connell said the team has no long-term concerns. Receiver Jordan Addison, lineman Jalen Redmond, cornerback Isaiah Rodgers and safety Harrison Smith were also listed as estimated non-participants. Coverage of the game itself said Darrisaw left with a shoulder issue and Ryan Van De Mark replaced him.

stories.text: Justin Jefferson chases Julio Jones on the all-time list
stories.summary: Jefferson needs 22 receiving yards to pass Julio Jones for fifth-most through a player's first seven seasons. He fumbled after a 25-yard gain against San Francisco, one of two Minnesota turnovers in the second half. Atlanta comes to town Sunday.

stories.text: 17 of 19: Brock Purdy's line against Minnesota's blitz
stories.summary: Purdy threw for 208 yards and two touchdowns against pressure on 20 dropbacks. The Vikings entered the night with the NFL's top scoring defense and gave up 21 first-half points. Defensive coordinator Brian Flores sent extra rushers and paid for it.

stories.text: Falcons at U.S. Bank Stadium, Sunday, 1 p.m. ET on FOX
stories.summary: Minnesota hosts a 3-7 Atlanta team, and five of the Vikings' seven remaining games are at home. Cousins returns to face the team that released him. All five NFL.com analysts pick Minnesota, a 7-point favorite on one book.

teams.name: Atlanta Falcons
teams.headline: Falcons face old friend Cousins in Minnesota

stories.text: Falcons prep for Kirk Cousins and the Vikings
stories.summary: Atlanta comes off its bye at 3-7 and visits 7-3 Minnesota on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET. The Vikings are now led by Kirk Cousins, whom the Falcons released in March and who joined Minnesota in a Nov. 10 trade. Coach Kevin Stefanski said Cousins looks like himself, and Cousins has two starts for his new team.

stories.text: Bergeron and Hellams in doubt, Branch still sidelined
stories.summary: Guard Matthew Bergeron (back) and safety DeMarcco Hellams (foot) did not practice and are listed as in doubt. Wide receiver Zachariah Branch (hamstring) has missed the past two games and sat out again, as did Jahan Dotson (hamstring) and Billy Bowman (hamstring). Pass rusher James Pearce Jr. (back) was limited.

stories.text: Jake Matthews carries the longest streak in the league
stories.summary: The 34-year-old left tackle is in his 13th season and has started 206 games, all but one of Atlanta's games since 2014. His run of 205 straight starts is a franchise record and the longest among active NFL players. He is also the only Falcon who has played through all eight years of the playoff drought.

stories.text: 36.4%: how often Minnesota's opponents blitz Penix
stories.summary: Michael Penix Jr. has faced a blitz on 36.4 percent of his dropbacks, fourth most in the league, and has completed 48 of 90 passes against it. Minnesota blitzes on 72.2 percent of opposing pass plays, far above the next team at 43.9 percent. The Falcons rank second worst in scoring over Penix's past three starts.

stories.text: At Minnesota on Sunday, 1 p.m. ET on Fox
stories.summary: The Falcons visit U.S. Bank Stadium for a 1 p.m. ET kickoff on Fox. Watch how Atlanta handles a Vikings defense that leads the league in pressure rate at 46.2 percent. A win would keep the Falcons within sight of Carolina, which leads the division by two games.

teams.name: Carolina Panthers
teams.headline: Panthers lead the division at .500

stories.text: Panthers hold the NFC South lead at 5-5
stories.summary: Carolina beat Baltimore 35-33 and sits two games clear of Atlanta, Tampa Bay and New Orleans. It is the first time since Week 7 that any team in the division has reached .500. The Panthers have won two straight after a three game losing streak.

stories.text: Ekwonu still out, Moton missing most of the year
stories.summary: Left tackle Ikem Ekwonu has not returned from an Achilles injury, and right tackle Taylor Moton has missed most of the season. Cornerback Mike Jackson is back from injured reserve ahead of Monday's trip to Tampa Bay. Both tackle spots remain thin against a Bucs pass rush led by Yaya Diaby.

stories.text: Chuba Hubbard runs for 120 and two scores
stories.summary: Hubbard rushed for 120 yards and two touchdowns against the Ravens. He has 831 rushing yards, sixth in the NFL, and 11 total touchdowns. Tampa Bay will see a rushing attack that has carried Carolina while Bryce Young works through turnovers.

stories.text: 14: Bryce Young's career game-winning drives
stories.summary: Young moved Carolina 55 yards in the fourth quarter, and Ryan Fitzgerald kicked a 37-yard field goal with 1:44 left. It was the 14th game-winning drive of Young's career. He finished with 254 yards, two touchdowns and one interception, and coach Dave Canales said he wants the ball in Young's hands in big moments.

stories.text: At Tampa Bay on Monday, 8:15 p.m. ET on ESPN
stories.summary: Carolina visits Raymond James Stadium on Monday Night Football. The Panthers have not won in Tampa since 2017, and the Bucs have won 11 of the last 13 meetings. Carolina has lost 10 fumbles this year, tied for the most in the league.

teams.name: New Orleans Saints
teams.headline: Saints drop another one-score game, 3-7

stories.text: Saints lose a second straight one-score game
stories.summary: New Orleans fell 21-13 to Chicago in Week 11 and sits at 3-7, two games behind Carolina. Both of the Saints' recent losses came by one possession. They travel to Cincinnati on Sunday needing to fix an offense that ranks 21st in scoring.

stories.text: Juwan Johnson misses Wednesday practice
stories.summary: Tight end Juwan Johnson (hamstring, wrist) did not practice Wednesday. Center Erik McCoy (biceps), guard David Edwards (hamstring), tackles Taliese Fuaga and Asim Richards (knees) and linebacker Pete Werner (hamstring) were limited. Cornerback Martin Emerson Jr. (concussion) took part fully.

stories.text: Chris Olave leads the Saints with 866 yards
stories.summary: Olave has 68 catches for 866 yards on 101 targets, the team's top receiving numbers. Devaugh Vele is next with 44 catches for 455 yards. Quarterback Tyler Shough has thrown 16 touchdowns and been sacked 29 times.

stories.text: 93.1: Saints rushing yards per game
stories.summary: New Orleans averages 93.1 rushing yards per game, fifth fewest in the league. Travis Etienne Jr. posted season highs of 14 carries and 76 yards last week after returning from a hamstring injury that cost him five games. Quarterback Tyler Shough leads the team with 221 rushing yards.

stories.text: At Cincinnati on Sunday, 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: The Saints face the 7-3 Bengals, who rank 30th in rushing at 79.4 yards per game. New Orleans allows 131.4 rushing yards per game, so the run game on both sides decides a lot. Watch whether Juwan Johnson plays.

teams.name: Tampa Bay Buccaneers
teams.headline: Bucs have no mulligans left vs Carolina

stories.text: Bowles says Bucs have no mulligans left
stories.summary: Tampa Bay is 3-7 after close losses in Chicago and Detroit and hosts first place Carolina on Monday. A win would pull the Bucs within one game of the division lead and give them the season sweep. A loss would leave them three games back with six to play.

stories.text: Parrish returns to practice, Morrison sits
stories.summary: Cornerback Jacob Parrish returned to practice Wednesday after hurting his back in Detroit, and defensive tackle Elijah Simmons returned from a concussion. Cornerback Benjamin Morrison did not practice. Linebacker Josiah Trotter sat out as well, and coach Todd Bowles called him sore and expects him to practice later in the week.

stories.text: Bucky Irving anchors the running game
stories.summary: Irving has 1,031 scrimmage yards this season. He and Kenneth Gainwell combined for 258 rushing yards in the 43-13 win at Carolina on Oct. 25. With the passing game struggling, the Bucs lean on the ground attack again against a Panthers defense ranked 26th against the run.

stories.text: 0-6: Tampa Bay's record without a turnover edge
stories.summary: The Bucs are 3-1 when they win the turnover battle and 0-6 when they do not. They forced no takeaways in Detroit. Carolina has lost 10 fumbles, tied for the most in the league.

stories.text: Vs Carolina on Monday, 8:15 p.m. ET on ESPN
stories.summary: Tampa Bay hosts the Panthers at Raymond James Stadium on Monday Night Football. Baker Mayfield is 6-1 against his former team and has thrown a touchdown in 18 of his past 19 primetime games. The Bucs are 2-10 in primetime games with Mayfield.

teams.name: Arizona Cardinals
teams.headline: Johnson likely starts again as Beck's back lingers

stories.text: Josh Johnson set for another start as Carson Beck's back flares
stories.summary: Coach Mike LaFleur said Wednesday that Josh Johnson is preparing to start Sunday against Washington. Rookie Carson Beck missed the loss in Kansas City and sat out practice again with back spasms. Friday's injury report will show whether Beck has a chance to return.

stories.text: Gaines setback, Beck out of practice, rest days for veterans
stories.summary: Guard Jon Gaines II suffered an ankle setback and will likely miss his sixth straight game. Beck did not practice Wednesday with his back issue. Budda Baker, Isaac Seumalo, Hjalte Froholdt and Josh Sweat sat out as rest or injury management, and linebacker Cody Simon (calf) was limited.

stories.text: Johnson, 40, throws for 155 yards in Kansas City
stories.summary: Josh Johnson went 18 of 31 for 155 yards and one touchdown in the 34-7 loss to the Chiefs. Kansas City sacked him three times, and he finished with an 82.1 passer rating. He had joined the roster less than two weeks earlier.

stories.text: 4: starting quarterbacks the Cardinals used in four weeks
stories.summary: Johnson became the fourth different starter in four weeks, after Jacoby Brissett, Gardner Minshew and Beck. Minshew is lost for the season with a right UCL injury. Arizona now sits at 3-8.

stories.text: Commanders visit Sunday, 4:25 PM ET on Fox
stories.summary: Arizona hosts Washington (4-5-1) at State Farm Stadium on Sunday, Nov. 29, with kickoff at 4:25 PM ET on Fox. Watch the quarterback situation first: Johnson is preparing to start unless Beck clears his back issue. Gaines and the offensive line depth also bear watching.

teams.name: Los Angeles Rams
teams.headline: Corum's 184 yards lift Rams past Packers

stories.text: Rams beat Packers 26-13 for fifth straight win
stories.summary: Los Angeles won the NFL's first Thanksgiving Eve game and moved to 7-4. The Rams held Green Bay to two first downs after halftime and picked off Jordan Love twice. The win keeps them in the NFC playoff chase.

stories.text: Kobie Turner returns from IR, Avila and Shelton out
stories.summary: Defensive end Kobie Turner (groin) was activated off injured reserve and practiced fully with no designation. Offensive linemen Steve Avila and Coleman Shelton (both hamstring) were ruled out for the Packers game. Tight end Terrance Ferguson (ankle) is on injured reserve for the rest of the season.

stories.text: Blake Corum runs for a career-high 184 yards
stories.summary: Corum carried 32 times for 184 yards and a touchdown, both career highs for carries and yards. He ran for 151 of those yards and the score after halftime, which let the Rams grind the clock. Matthew Stafford threw only eight passes in the second half.

stories.text: 2: first downs Green Bay gained after halftime
stories.summary: The Packers managed two first downs after the break while the Rams leaned on the run. Love finished 17 of 29 for 198 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions. Micah Parsons recorded his first sack of the season in his return from a torn ACL.

stories.text: Chiefs on Thursday Night Football, Dec. 3
stories.summary: The Rams host Kansas City (8-2) at SoFi Stadium in Week 13 on Thursday, Dec. 3, at 8:15 PM ET on Prime Video. Los Angeles will have a short week after playing Wednesday. Watch whether the run game that carried Corum holds up against a tougher front.

teams.name: San Francisco 49ers
teams.headline: Purdy's ankle clouds Seahawks showdown

stories.text: Purdy's ankle leaves Seahawks game in doubt
stories.summary: Brock Purdy did not practice Wednesday after hurting his ankle in the second quarter of the win over Minnesota. Kyle Shanahan called it a low ankle issue, not a high sprain, and said Purdy is day to day. Shanahan said there is a possibility Purdy sits Sunday, in which case Mac Jones starts.

stories.text: Evans, Greenlaw, Neal and Watkins miss Wednesday practice
stories.summary: Receiver Mike Evans (Achilles), receiver Jordan Watkins (groin), safety Siran Neal (knee, foot) and Purdy did not practice. Cornerback Deommodore Lenoir (foot) was limited. Christian McCaffrey and Trent Williams were listed as resting.

stories.text: Purdy went 21 of 26 for 255 yards and three scores
stories.summary: Purdy threw three touchdowns with no interceptions in the 35-10 win over the Vikings in Week 11. He then left the field with the ankle injury and finished the game. He has thrown for 2,624 yards this season.

stories.text: 23: touchdown passes for Purdy through 10 games
stories.summary: That total ranks third in the league, per Heavy, and goes with 2,624 passing yards. San Francisco is 9-1 and leads the NFC West. Purdy's status for Sunday is the main variable.

stories.text: Seahawks come to Santa Clara Sunday, 4:25 PM ET on Fox
stories.summary: San Francisco hosts Seattle (6-4) in Week 12 on Sunday, Nov. 29, at 4:25 PM ET on Fox. Seattle expects Sam Darnold back at quarterback. Purdy's practice work Thursday and Friday will decide whether Mac Jones starts.

teams.name: Seattle Seahawks
teams.headline: Darnold eyes return against the 49ers

stories.text: Darnold set to return against the 49ers
stories.summary: Sam Darnold missed two games with a quadriceps injury and a cracked rib suffered in the Nov. 2 loss to the Bears. Mike Macdonald said starting him is the plan if practice goes well, and Darnold returned to practice Wednesday. The offensive line also changes: Charles Cross is expected back at left tackle.

stories.text: Lucas and Nelson out, Cross expected back
stories.summary: Right tackle Abraham Lucas (ankle) is out, with a timeline of days to weeks, and he is not going on injured reserve. Guard Quenton Nelson is out this week after a knee procedure and could return next week. Defensive tackle Leonard Williams was limited with a stinger after missing two games.

stories.text: Drew Lock won both starts in Darnold's absence
stories.summary: Lock completed 73 percent of his passes for 415 yards and three touchdowns with no interceptions across two starts. He also lost two fumbles. Seattle went 2-0 in those games and sits at 6-4.

stories.text: 867: Jaxon Smith-Njigba's receiving yards through Week 7
stories.summary: Smith-Njigba had 9 catches for 150 yards and a touchdown in the 20-3 win over the Chiefs on Oct. 25, his sixth 100-yard game in seven weeks. His 867 yards were third most through seven games in the Super Bowl era and led the NFL. This figure is from that Week 7 article, so the season total is higher now.

stories.text: At the 49ers Sunday, 4:25 PM ET on Fox
stories.summary: Seattle (6-4) visits San Francisco (9-1) on Sunday, Nov. 29, at 4:25 PM ET on Fox. Darnold's health and Purdy's ankle shape both sides of this NFC West game. Seattle plays the Rams twice later this season, so the division race stays live.
